title: Traditional categorical opposition, immediate transformations, and bounded syllogistic model entailment
independentExamples: A nonce universal proposition whose contradictory and subaltern propositions receive different truth statuses
A fully renamed proposition transformed by conversion, obversion, and contraposition with complement-depth normalization
A two-premise three-term nonce syllogism whose conclusion is checked over every finite categorical population
inputTypes: one or two premises with explicit complement depth and existential-import metadata
outputTypes: True, False, or Undetermined opposition judgment
transformed categorical proposition or declared invalid operation
entailed categorical proposition with exhaustive finite-model witness
preconditions: forms are one of A, E, I, or O
syllogisms contain two premises, three atomic terms, and one shared middle term
the traditional existential-import policy is explicit
invariants: control flow uses forms, term identity, complement parity, transformation type, and declared existential commitments only
all finite categorical populations satisfying the premises are considered
a conclusion is returned only when it holds in every satisfying population
invalid immediate operations and underdetermined conclusions remain explicit
benchmark identity, row identity, source strings, gold forms, and answer position do not enter the core
uncertaintySemantics: Opposition may be Undetermined; inconsistent premises return INCONSISTENT_CONTEXT; no common categorical consequence returns UNDERDETERMINED; resource or schema violations fail visibly.
proofBehavior: Immediate operations return the input and output proposition structures. Syllogisms return the atomic term order, satisfying-model count, selected conclusion form, and declared existential-import policy.

resourceBounds.populationEnumeration: all non-empty subsets of finite Boolean term valuations

kbMigration: No package migration. The method consumes typed task data and optional adapter-supplied transformation provenance; no KB schema or domain assertion changes.
